noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

endpoint.description:
Use to specify the path at the top level. This essentially creates an alias for the type name.
If not specified, the type name is used as the path. This must be unique across all types.

subPath.description:
Use to specify the sub-path and how the components are mapped to arguments.
For example `pathSpec="type/:typeName"` will expect the sub-path `type` of the type name (or the path if
specified) and everything within it to be passed as the `typeName` parameter of the action.

paramsArg.description:
Use to specify a field name or an object name which query parameters apply to.
If not specified, query parameters are matched to function arguments or type fields if the argument is an object.

postBody.description:
Use to specify that the JSON body of a POST request will be deserialized for this argument. Only a single method
parameter can receive the body this way and this only works for JSON bodies. (Other parameters will not be able
to receive values from POST requests.)

serveContent.description:
Use to specify that the result of the action should be served directly as HTTP content.
This only applies to functions that return a ContentValue object, which has everything necessary to produce
the HTTP response.

@see Content

unwrapContentValue.description:
Use to specify that a returned ContentValue object should be unwrapped to give only the inner content in the
response. Invalid for functions that do not return a ContentValue object.

additionalHeaders.description:
Use to specify the additional headers on the HTTP response. Note the header(s) specified here can override the
existing header(s) in the response.
For example, `headers={"OData-Version":"4.0","content-type":"application/xml"}`

title:
The `@restful` annotation specifies how C3 type methods can be called through the REST API. All methods can be
called using the standard API mechanisms, but in addition types can create custom URLs using GET and REST-style
argument extraction rather than POST requests.

Types can expose an endpoint path with one or more functions mapped to sub-paths of that endpoint. Because all type
endpoints need to coexist, it is best practice to use a separate endpoint path once on the type and specify the
sub-path for each function.

```c3typ
@restful(endpoint='milk')
type Milkmaid {

  @restful(subPath='cow/:fat')
  cowMilk: function(fat: !string)

  @restful(subPath='goat')
  goatMilk: function()
}
```

In the example above, `/milk/cow/skim` will be mapped to `Milkmaid.cowMilk`, with "skim" passed to the
function argument while `/milk/goat` will be mapped to `Milkmaid.goatMilk`.

Note:
  1. overloaded methods should not be used with #subPath
  2. the first matching method is chosen so they should be ordered in decreasing specificity

If the handler needs more information than just the query parameters, it is possible to get the entire request
by declaring a method parameter of type {@link HttpRequest}. It's also possible to build the entire response by
declaring the method return value as {@link HttpResponse} or {@link Content}.

Note that a custom endpoint may also be created by mixing in the {@link Restful} type. That works well for endpoints
with custom handling that want to consume a raw request and produce a complete response.
